title: Wire native pre-release gate and evidence-based verdict
description:
Objective: finish Gates D and E in docs/pre-release-test-plan.md: orchestrate the workflow, contention, recovery, and release-asset suites against the exact candidate bytes on native CI runners, then make a Luna High agent issue a repeatable evidence-backed verdict. Read the completed QA runner/report schema, verify scripts, GoReleaser config, CI/release workflows, docs/release-assets.md, and docs/release-qa.md before editing.

Entry points: add a documented prerelease mode to Unix and PowerShell verification with explicit --seed, --repeat, --report, --keep-workdir, and candidate/artifact inputs. Fast commit mode must remain fast. Prerelease must run formatting, unit/integration, vet, race where supported, workflow matrix, 20-iteration contention, fault/recovery, GoReleaser validation, asset contract, native install/workflow, and updater matrix. One nonzero scenario must make the command nonzero while still finalizing a readable report.

Candidate identity: build all six standalone artifacts once, record each digest and embedded version/commit/build date, and pass those exact files to downstream jobs. Do not validate one snapshot and silently rebuild different publish bytes. Prefer a GitHub Actions artifact promoted to the publish job; if GoReleaser cannot publish prebuilt bytes safely, add a documented reproducibility comparison and block on any unexplained digest/metadata difference. Preserve checksum and stable-filename contract.

Native platform matrix: execute the matching candidate on Linux amd64, Windows amd64, and macOS (amd64 or arm64 as available). Each runner must download/verify the candidate digest, execute the lifecycle subset in a temp repo, and upload its JSON shard and failure artifacts. On Windows, wait for and verify the deferred updater helper success and rollback/error-file cases; cross-compilation does not count. Record unsupported shipped architectures as compile/format/checksum coverage, not native execution. Merge shards only after verifying the same commit/candidate set/seed/schema.

Evaluator contract: add a detailed, model-ready instruction template for GPT-5.6 Luna High. It must read the merged JSON and retained artifacts, verify required scenario IDs and minimum iterations/process counts, candidate digests, native platforms, preservation manifests, checkout isolation, unexplained skips/timeouts/retries, and normalized repeat consistency. It writes pre-release-verdict.md containing candidate identity, evidence paths, scenario/platform totals, failures/skips, residual risks, and exactly one GO, NO_GO, or INCONCLUSIVE verdict. Failed assertions force NO_GO; missing/unreadable evidence or required native coverage forces INCONCLUSIVE; only complete evidence can yield GO. Add a deterministic programmatic preflight so the agent cannot waive structural omissions.

CI safety: prerelease validation must happen before publication, use least privilege, have explicit job timeouts, upload reports on success and failure, avoid secrets in artifacts, and never update a real installation. Add a manually dispatchable prerelease workflow if tag validation cannot be tested safely before a tag. Keep network access limited to tool/artifact acquisition and the explicit published-release mode; workflow tests stay loopback-only.

Execution acceptance: run the entire prerelease gate for the current commit, including two same-seed normalized comparisons and all locally available native scenarios. Inspect the report and produce a sample verdict using the exact evaluator template; deliberately remove a required shard/assertion and prove preflight/evaluation becomes INCONCLUSIVE rather than GO. Existing commit and release commands remain compatible. Validate workflow YAML and document runtimes/tool versions, rerun commands, artifact retention, and release operator steps. Completion comment must include commit, candidate digests, CI run/report links or local paths, platform/scenario/iteration totals, durations, all skips/retries, sample verdict, and residual risks.
